statement: A wall is 4.5 m long and 2.4 m high. It needs two coats of paint. One litre of paint covers 12 square metres, and paint is sold only in 0.5-litre tins. How many tins must be bought?

choices.misconception: I worked out the litres of paint needed and gave that, not the number of tins.
I forgot that the wall needs two coats, so I worked out 1.8 tins and bought 2.
I found 3.6 tins and rounded down, which leaves part of the second coat unpainted.
I divided correctly but forgot that tins can only be bought whole.

hints: What exactly is being counted in the answer?
Find the area, double it for two coats, change square metres into litres, then litres into tins. Before answering, re-read: tins come whole.
The area is $10.8\text{ m}^2$, two coats make $21.6\text{ m}^2$, which needs $1.8$ litres, that is $3.6$ tins.

solutions.reliable: The wall has area $4.5 \times 2.4 = 10.8\text{ m}^2$. Two coats cover $21.6\text{ m}^2$, which needs $21.6 \div 12 = 1.8$ litres. Each tin holds $0.5$ litres, so $1.8 \div 0.5 = 3.6$ tins of paint are used. Three tins are not enough, so 4 tins must be bought. The transferable idea: before answering, check the units and whether the answer has to be a whole number.

whyOnTest: Each step is easy; the marks are lost on the second coat, the unit of the answer and rounding up to whole tins.
